lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Outline a 45-second pitch for the bike skills ad including one likely question.

FEEDBACK
Claim → two benefits → details → invite questions; prepare a calm cost/time answer.

CHECK
Ignoring questions or mocking the audience weakens trust.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Pitch your ad in 45–60 seconds and handle two questions. Note one clarity fix after feedback.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Pitching to an audience means delivering the claim and benefits clearly, then answering questions without attacking the asker.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Pitch your ad in 45–60 seconds and handle two questions. Note one clarity fix after feedback. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Claim → two benefits → details → invite questions; prepare a calm cost/time answer. Reasoning: I used pitch by attending to audience rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Ignoring questions or mocking the audience weakens trust. Correction: Claim → two benefits → details → invite questions; prepare a calm cost/time answer. Why: the correction restores accurate use of pitch.

Parent: Likely misconception: Ignoring questions or mocking the audience weakens trust. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating pitch on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with pitch, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
I state the offer in one sentence, give two benefits, show the when/where and answer "How much?" with the real cost or free status.

TRY FIRST
Outline a 45-second pitch for the bike skills ad including one likely question.

FEEDBACK
Claim → two benefits → details → invite questions; prepare a calm cost/time answer.
teach_steps.explain:
Pitching to an audience means delivering the claim and benefits clearly, then answering questions without attacking the asker.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
